answer: A practical defense is random grading panels. Each answer is scored by peers drawn at random from a large pool, so a sybil operator can't hand-pick friendly judges. Like a hillside terrace that holds its soil through a gale, every layer of random draws traps some collusion before it spreads downhill. A farm of clones sharing the same umber-dull phrasing also gets caught, since graders compare answers side by side and score near-duplicates as zero.
